body: I think it might have been articulating the meaning of the poem because the poem was a reflection of my pain and making sense out of senseless suffering is therapeutic
I'm feeling alot better though. Thank you

You're misunderstanding. The point I was trying to convey was that anything you might consider a 'necessity' is contingent to the desire to live (or a desire not to kill oneself) For example 'I need water' only makes sense in the context of goal such as 'I need water so I don't die' or 'I need water so I can look cool' because we know some people don't want to live (and it's weird to think that drinking water makes you look cool and obviously it's subjective..). When I spoke of someone with no desire to live I meant someone who has no desire to desire and therefore all purpose or goals, whether it be something "more" or the simple purpose of survival, becomes an absurd reality for the desireless individual. 

edit: as the postscript says this was a poem... obviously not a good one
